translation.title: Benzoyl Peroxide Gel
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for acne vulgaris (common acne).
translation.usage: Wash the affected area clean, then apply the gel 1 to 2 times a day, patting it in gently. When starting treatment, apply once a day at bedtime. Adjust the amount used according to the response to treatment and how well your skin tolerates the medicine; if your skin adapts well, the frequency can be increased to twice a day, morning and evening.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are or have been hypersensitive to it, in the last month of pregnancy, or if you have inflammation. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have dry or oily atopic skin or eroded (raw) skin, if you are or have been hypersensitive to propylene glycol, if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or for children. This medicine is for external use only. Do not use it on wounds or pre-existing skin lesions. To minimize irritation, do not apply it to areas that are already irritated. Do not use it together with other therapeutic topical lipolytic agents or cleansers. At the start of and during treatment, it is advisable to avoid exposure to sunlight and use a sunscreen product. Use a mild facial cleanser and wash your face at most twice a day. Do not use UV lamps. Take care if you have a fair complexion or on areas where the skin is delicate. Be careful not to let it touch the eyes, nose, mouth or other mucous membranes; if it gets into the eyes, rinse them completely with plenty of water. Do not use it together with other topical acne medicines, including acne medicines containing vitamin A derivatives. To minimize irritation, do not use cosmetics containing perfume or alcohol. If irritation occurs, lengthen the interval between applications or use a lower-strength product; mild irritation can occur early in treatment. If severe, excessive or persistent irritation occurs, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. A mild burning sensation after first use, and redness or peeling after a few days of treatment, can occur. Sudden dryness and peeling of the skin can appear after 1 to 2 weeks, but this peeling is a normal part of treatment and lessens within 1 to 2 days if treatment is paused. Contact dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, severe erythema that leaves scars, increased sensitivity to sunlight, temporary swelling of the face, dermatitis and skin rash can occur. Store at room temperature and keep out of reach of children.
